description: We are a team of young Python coders from theCoderSchool Scarsdale participating virtually in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our goal is to use our programming skills, creativity, and teamwork to develop a fun and educational project related to space exploration.
summary:
We, The CoderSchool Space Coders, present Return to Earth! 
Return to Earth is a text-based game where the Player is returning from a trip to Mars; their return takes 7 days to complete, so they must manage their resources and make sure all is intact until then. 
As their shuttle heads towards Earth, they have a choice of: 
Repairing the ship’s systems.
Searching storage for supplies.
Growing food in the hydroponics bay.
Resting in their cabin.
Running the emergency water cycler. 
Each of these actions takes away either their oxygen, food, water, power, morale, or repair units; however, they gain more of another resource by doing so. 
At times, emergencies may occur, further bringing down their resources. Being prepared for these is the best they can do, as not having any resources left can result in a Game Over! 
If the player made it through all seven days, a score is calculated based on the resources they have left at the end of the game.
details: The project is a game which involves an astronaut flying on a spacecraft from Mars to head back home to Earth. The return takes seven days, during which time the player controls different choices the astronaut must make in order to manage supplies like power, oxygen, food, water, and other resources. The player must also use quick thinking to deal with random emergencies which affect certain stats. The project is intended to give players a glimpse of the responsibilities an astronaut has aboard a spacecraft. It also encourages replayability, so players can explore different choices and how they affect the flow of the game. Our team tried to consider a wide range of random events and emergencies that could plausibly affect a space mission, and got creative with implementing these different emergencies. There are a total of ten emergencies that the player can face, with each affecting unique stats. Some of these emergencies include a navigation error which lowers morale, an electrical shortage which lowers power, and an asteroid collision damaging equipment which then needs to be repaired. The project was coded entirely in Python, using the website CodePad to work on a single file together as a team.
